author: sjm41
body:
* **ARBA rule (ID and label):**
ARBA00022801 & ARBA00022912

* **Sequences with problematic annotation (ID + gene/protein name):**
Dmel blistery (FBgn0000244) Q9VHC3

* **Description of issue**

ARBA00022801 -> hydrolase KW -> hydrolase activity (GO:0016787)
InterPro signature IPR006020
InterPro signature IPR013625
InterPro signature IPR035012


ARBA00022912 -> Protein phosphatase KW -> phosphoprotein phosphatase activity (GO:0004721)
InterPro signature IPR000980
InterPro signature IPR006020
InterPro signature IPR035012

But 'blistery' encodes Dmel tensin, and like most tensions, it's characterised to act as an adapter/scaffold protein and not have phosphatase activity. In fact, Dmel blistery even lacks the phosphatase-like domain (PMID [15030759](http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/15030759/))
title: ARBA2GO issue: ARBA00022801 & ARBA00022912

author: Antonialock
body:
so there seems to be evidence that some tensins have phosphatase activity (e.g. https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30092354 - I have only looked at the abstract). Some tensins like tensin 4 and drosphila blistery do not have the phosphatase domain (but tensin 4 does not have IPR035012 which is part of the rule).

I will curate blistery, so it becomes part of this conditions set
https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb?query=%28xref%3Ainterpro-IPR006020%29+AND+%28xref%3Ainterpro-IPR013625%29+AND+%28xref%3Ainterpro-IPR035012%29
